DE1 · Data Engineering · Streaming

Real-Time Kafka + Spark Transaction Monitoring

Problem

Streaming transaction systems must handle duplicate deliveries and mid-stream crashes without losing data or counting the same transaction twice. Exactly-once behaviour is the hard part — not just consuming messages.

Architecture

Kafka topic → Spark Structured Streaming consumer → deduplication on transaction ID with watermarking → checkpointed state store → aggregated monitoring tables. A crash-recovery test kills the job mid-run and restarts from checkpoint.

What I built

  • Kafka producer replaying a transaction stream with intentionally injected duplicates
  • Spark Structured Streaming job with dropDuplicates + checkpointing
  • Crash-recovery harness: kill, restart, reconcile counts
  • 5 automated tests covering dedup, recovery, and counts

Code — Spark deduplication

stream = (spark.readStream.format("kafka") .option("subscribe", "transactions") .load()) txns = parse_transactions(stream) deduped = (txns .withWatermark("event_time", "10 minutes") .dropDuplicates(["transaction_id"])) # checkpointing gives 0 lost / 0 duplicates # after a crash-restart from last checkpoint

Tech stack

KafkaPySpark / Spark StreamingPythonpytest

Honest label: verified in a local run (60,000 messages). The PySpark job is deploy-ready for a cluster; the verified numbers are from the local run, not a production cluster.

Data Engineering · Fraud Detection

Real-Time E-Commerce Fraud & Transaction Monitoring

Problem

Card fraud hides inside legitimate transaction volume. Batch reports find it a day late. This engine scores every transaction against a 5-rule detection system as it arrives.

Architecture

Transaction generator (100,670 txns, 2,000 customers, 7 days) → streaming rules engine (velocity, amount, geography and behaviour rules) → incident grouping → precision / recall evaluation → SQL analysis (12 queries) + Power BI spec with DAX measures.

What I built

  • 5-rule streaming detection engine in Python
  • Rule tuning that cut false positives from 105 → 15 (v3)
  • Incident-level evaluation — catching the fraud incident, not just single txns
  • 12 SQL queries, Power BI dashboard spec + DAX, AWS architecture doc

Code — rules engine (excerpt)

def score(txn, history): flags = [] if txn.amount > 3 * history.median_amount: flags.append("AMOUNT_SPIKE") if history.txns_last_hour >= 5: flags.append("VELOCITY") if txn.country != history.home_country: flags.append("GEO_MISMATCH") return "FLAG" if len(flags) >= 2 else "CLEAR"

DE2 · Data Engineering · Cloud

AWS ETL Pipeline with Airflow, S3, Glue & Redshift

Problem

Raw extracts contain duplicates, corrupt rows and schema breaks. A pipeline that silently drops bad rows — or double-loads on retry — destroys trust in every downstream dashboard.

Architecture

Source files → Amazon S3 raw zone → AWS Glue validation & transform → Amazon Redshift load, orchestrated by Apache Airflow. Bad records go to a quarantine path with reasons; loads are idempotent by file + key.

What I built

  • Ingestion + validation with explicit quarantine (980 rows)
  • Idempotent load logic — re-running loads 0 extra rows
  • Corrupt-file retry path, proven in tests
  • Data-quality checks at every stage; 5 automated tests

Code — idempotent load check

-- Load only keys not already in Redshift INSERT INTO warehouse.orders SELECT * FROM staging.orders s WHERE NOT EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM warehouse.orders w WHERE w.order_id = s.order_id ); -- Result: safe to re-run the DAG any time

Tech stack

DA1 · Data Analytics · BI

E-Commerce Sales & Revenue Analytics

Problem

Headline revenue growth masked a collapsing category and money-losing promotions. The business needed category- and product-level truth, not totals.

Architecture

50,906 orders → SQL + Python (pandas) analysis → category trend, margin and promotion analysis → Power BI dashboard with DAX measures.

What I built

  • Category revenue trend analysis that surfaced the Home & Kitchen decline
  • Promotion margin analysis finding negative-margin products
  • Dashboard + DAX measures for revenue, margin and category mix
  • 7 automated tests on the analysis pipeline

Code — SQL category trend

SELECT category, SUM(revenue) AS revenue, SUM(revenue) * 1.0 / SUM(SUM(revenue)) OVER () AS share FROM orders GROUP BY category ORDER BY revenue DESC; -- Home & Kitchen: -36.81% period over period

DA2 · Data Analytics · ML

Customer Churn & Retention Analytics

Problem

At 26.1% churn, spreading retention offers evenly wastes spend. The team needed a scored risk tier so offers target the customers — and revenue — most at risk.

Architecture

10,000 customers → feature engineering in Python → NumPy logistic regression (built from scratch, no black-box library) → risk tiers → Power BI retention view.

What I built

  • Logistic regression implemented in NumPy with AUC evaluation
  • Risk tiering: high-risk tier isolated at 2,075 customers
  • Revenue-at-risk quantification for the high-risk tier
  • 3 automated tests

Code — Python / NumPy model

import numpy as np def sigmoid(z): return 1/(1+np.exp(-z)) # gradient descent on standardized features proba = sigmoid(X @ w + b) # AUC = 0.8901 on held-out customers high_risk = proba >= 0.7 # 2,075 customers
